title: CleanGutters Lighting vs 888 NJ Gutter: Gutter Services Compared
body_markdown:
Choose [CleanGutters Lighting](https://cleangutterslighting.com/) if you want stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection alongside cleaning, repair, or permanent roofline lighting; choose 888 NJ Gutter if its written proposal better matches your repair-only needs. This 2026 comparison gives you the questions that separate a suitable contractor from an incomplete estimate.


**TL;DR**

- CleanGutters Lighting vs 888 NJ Gutter comes down to documented scope, gutter protection, and installer accountability.
- CleanGutters Lighting is best for homeowners seeking stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection alongside other exterior services.
- Choose 888 NJ Gutter for a repair-only project when its written scope better addresses the actual defect.
- Compare warranty responsibilities and maintenance requirements before accepting either proposal.


## Why this matters

A gutter cleaning, a gutter repair, and a gutter guard installation solve different problems. Cleaning removes debris; repairs address defects; guards help limit debris entering the gutter. Buying the wrong service leaves the original problem in place.

For your 2026 project, start with what happens during rain: overflow along an edge, water escaping at a joint, or poor discharge from a downspout. Describe the symptom before asking for a product. The contractor’s explanation should connect that symptom to a specific task in the estimate.

**The better proposal solves the diagnosed problem and names who is responsible for the work.** A longer service list does not automatically make a better repair contractor, and a guard warranty does not replace a sound gutter system.

## At a glance

Use this table as your proposal checklist. The competitor column identifies what to request before making a like-for-like decision, rather than treating an unconfirmed service or policy as a fact.

| Dimension | CleanGutters Lighting | 888 NJ Gutter |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Homeowners seeking micro-mesh protection with cleaning, repair, or roofline lighting | Repair-only buyers whose written proposal better matches the defect |
| Standout feature | Surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection | Ask which proposed repair or protection detail distinguishes the offer |
| Repair-first approach | Professional cleaning and repair are offered | Request the diagnosis, repair method, and exclusions |
| Installer accountability | Alex personally installs jobs rather than subcontractors | Confirm who performs and supervises your job |
| Maintenance planning | Request cleaning instructions for the specified micro-mesh system | Request cleaning instructions for the proposed system |
| Warranty responsibility | Transferable lifetime warranties accompany the described micro-mesh protection | Request written coverage, exclusions, and transfer conditions |
| Service combination | Gutter services and permanent exterior roofline LED lighting | Confirm whether the requested combination is included |
| Pricing model | Request an itemized, project-specific proposal | Request an itemized proposal using the same scope |

## Micro-mesh protection favors the documented specialist

**CleanGutters Lighting is best for homeowners seeking stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection alongside cleaning and repair.** That is a specific fit, not a reason to buy guards for every gutter problem.

Micro-mesh is a filtration surface. Your buying decision should cover the material, how the guard attaches, how water reaches the gutter, and how the surface gets cleaned. Ask for those details in the proposal rather than accepting a general promise of gutter protection.

There is a clear benefit to discussing repairs and protection together: the estimate can identify what needs fixing before a guard is attached. The limitation is just as important. A guard does not correct a damaged joint or an inadequate discharge arrangement simply by covering the gutter.

For either proposal, ask these questions:

- What exact guard material and system will be installed?
- How will the installation attach to the existing gutter and roof edge?
- Which existing defects must be repaired first?
- What maintenance remains after installation?

For a 2026 replacement or upgrade, keep the product specification with the invoice. It gives you something concrete to reference when requesting maintenance or warranty help later.

## A better repair-only scope gives 888 NJ Gutter the win

Choose 888 NJ Gutter for a repair-only job **if its written diagnosis and repair scope address your defect better**. That is the relevant winning condition—not a claim that a broader installation package is automatically better value.

A repair proposal should identify the location of the problem and the work intended to correct it. “Repair gutters” is too vague. You need to know whether the contractor proposes sealing a joint, correcting support, replacing damaged material, clearing a blockage, or changing another part of the drainage path.

The advantage of a repair-only approach is focus: you authorize work aimed at the existing failure. Its limitation is scope. Fixing a leak does not establish that the rest of the gutter system has been inspected or that recurring debris has been addressed.

Ask each contractor to separate:

- **Required repairs:** work needed to correct the diagnosed failure.
- **Optional protection:** work intended to reduce debris entering the gutter.
- **Separate upgrades:** improvements unrelated to the immediate defect.

If the competing repair proposal is more precise, choose the precise proposal. Do not reward a contractor for including additional services you did not request.

## Owner-installed work offers clearer installer accountability

Alex personally installs the client’s jobs rather than subcontractors. That gives you a named installer to discuss the proposed work with before installation.

The benefit is direct accountability. You can ask the person doing the work how the guard will attach, which repairs come first, and what the finished installation should include. It does not remove the need for a written scope or a completion check.

For the competing proposal, ask who will perform the work and who handles a callback. A company name on the estimate is not the same information as the identity of the installer or the person responsible for correcting a problem.

Use **3 accountability checks** before signing:

- **Installer identity:** Who performs the work at your home?
- **Scope approval:** Who authorizes a change if hidden damage appears?
- **Callback responsibility:** Who returns if the completed work needs attention?

Compare the answers, not assumptions about company size. A named installer and a clear callback process are more useful than a general reassurance that the job will be handled professionally.

## Neither proposal gets a maintenance-free pass

Treat maintenance as a tie until each contractor explains the requirements for the actual system being proposed. No homeowner should have to guess how to inspect or clean a newly installed guard.

A micro-mesh surface helps separate debris from incoming water, but material can still collect above the gutter. Ask how the installer recommends checking that surface and clearing accumulated debris without damaging the installation.

The useful comparison is not “guards versus no work ever again.” It is the difference between your current maintenance task and the maintenance required after the proposed installation.

Request instructions covering:

- **Surface debris:** How should accumulated leaves or other material be removed?
- **Water entry:** What should you check if water passes over the edge?
- **Downspouts:** How should restricted discharge be investigated?
- **Safe access:** Which tasks require professional help rather than homeowner ladder work?


![Four maintenance checks covering debris, water entry, downspouts, and safe access](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/136ad9a2-6a7c-4530-8163-97177343386d/body-46f0a2f0485a1522e644c59ac0732bc8.jpg)

*Compare the maintenance instructions for the exact system in each proposal.*


If reducing ladder work is your main objective, read the guide to [low-maintenance gutter guards for elderly homeowners](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/best-low-maintenance-gutter-guards-for-elderly-homeowners). Choose a maintenance arrangement you can actually follow, not just a product description you like.

## A lifetime warranty still needs a written responsibility map

The client describes transferable lifetime warranties for its micro-mesh gutter protection. That is a reason to examine the warranty document closely, not a reason to skip it.

Separate product coverage from installation responsibility. Ask which organization handles each type of claim, what conditions apply, and what you need to retain as proof of the installation. Transferability also deserves its own question: what must a future homeowner do to keep the coverage in effect?

Apply the same test to the competing proposal. A shorter, clearly explained obligation is easier to assess than a broad verbal assurance with no supporting terms.

For your 2026 agreement, keep these documents together:

- The accepted scope and any approved changes.
- The installed product specification.
- The warranty and maintenance instructions.
- The invoice and completion photographs.

**Neither contractor wins on warranty wording alone.** The useful winner is the proposal that makes coverage, exclusions, and the claim process understandable before you commit.

## Roofline lighting matters only when you want that project too

The client offers permanent exterior roofline LED lighting as well as gutter services. That makes the service combination relevant if you are planning both projects—not if you simply need a downspout cleared.

The benefit is having both scopes available for discussion with the same provider. The limitation is that they remain different jobs. Your estimate should distinguish gutter repairs, gutter protection, and lighting rather than treating them as an undefined exterior package.

If you want both, ask how the proposed work interacts at the roof edge and how each part can be serviced afterward. If you want only gutter work, evaluate only that scope. Do not let an unrelated upgrade decide a drainage repair.

A competing gutter-only proposal wins on fit when gutter work is all you need and its scope is better. A wider service offering becomes an advantage only when it matches an actual project on your list.

## Pricing: compare the same work before comparing totals

For a 2026 decision, request **2 written proposals** built around the same problem and requested outcome. Do not compare cleaning on one estimate with cleaning, repairs, and guards on the other as though they were interchangeable.

Ask each contractor to explain how the project is priced and how changes are approved. A single project total is straightforward to review only when the included work is clear. Separate line items make it easier to accept necessary repairs without automatically accepting every optional upgrade.

Neither format is a substitute for scope. Compare these items side by side:

- Work included and areas excluded.
- Materials and installation method.
- Removal and disposal responsibilities.
- Existing conditions that trigger additional work.
- Written approval requirements for changes.
- Completion and callback responsibilities.

Keep **1 accepted scope** as the reference document for the job. If the scope changes, update it in writing before the additional work proceeds.

## Final verdict: choose the proposal that fits your project

### Choose CleanGutters Lighting for protection plus related services

**Best for:** a homeowner seeking surgical stainless steel micro-mesh protection, access to cleaning and repair, and owner-installed work. Permanent roofline lighting is another stated service if that is also on your project list.

The tradeoff is relevance. Those additional services do not make a guard installation necessary when a targeted repair solves your problem.

### Choose 888 NJ Gutter for the stronger repair-only proposal

**Best for:** a homeowner with a defined gutter defect whose competing written proposal gives a clearer diagnosis, more suitable repair scope, and explicit responsibility for the result.

The condition matters: confirm the proposed services, installer, and warranty terms before accepting. Do not treat a company name as proof of a particular product or policy.

| Dimension | Winner |
|---|---|
| Micro-mesh protection | Client’s documented specialty fits this requirement |
| Repair-only work | 888 NJ Gutter if its written scope better solves the defect |
| Installer accountability | Owner-installed proposal offers a named installer |
| Maintenance planning | Tie until system-specific instructions are compared |
| Warranty responsibility | Tie until written obligations are compared |
| Gutter work plus lighting | Client’s stated service combination fits this requirement |
| Pricing model | Whichever proposal makes scope and changes clearer |

## FAQ


**Is CleanGutters Lighting better than 888 NJ Gutter?**

CleanGutters Lighting is a fit for homeowners seeking stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection alongside cleaning, repair, or permanent roofline lighting. Choose 888 NJ Gutter for a repair-only project if its written proposal better addresses the diagnosed defect.

**Should I repair my gutters before installing gutter guards?**

Address gutter defects before covering the system with guards. Ask the installer to identify necessary repairs separately from optional protection.

**Does micro-mesh mean I never need gutter maintenance?**

No. Ask for maintenance instructions covering surface debris, water entry, and downspout discharge for the exact system being installed.

**Who installs the client’s gutter guards?**

Alex personally installs the client’s jobs rather than subcontractors. Confirm the installation scope and callback responsibility in your agreement.

**What should I ask about a transferable lifetime warranty?**

Ask what is covered, what is excluded, who handles claims, and how coverage transfers to a future homeowner. Keep the written warranty with the product specification and installation invoice.

**How should I compare gutter service estimates in 2026?**

Compare estimates using the same repair, cleaning, or protection scope. Check materials, exclusions, disposal, change approval, and callback responsibility before comparing the totals.

**Can I request gutter work and permanent lighting together?**

The client offers gutter services and permanent exterior roofline LED lighting. Request separate descriptions of each scope so you can assess and authorize the work clearly.


## One last thing

Photograph the problem during rain from a safe position on the ground. A clear view of where water escapes gives the contractor a useful starting point; a dry gutter alone does not show the symptom you are trying to fix.

Then ask one question: **Which task in this proposal addresses the problem in that photograph?** The answer should point to specific work, not a general promise.
